translation: The Lingshu says: When the five grains enter the stomach, their dregs, fluids (jinye), and ancestral-qi (zongqi) become the three passageways (sansui). Therefore the ancestral-qi accumulates in the chest, issues from the throat, in order to penetrate through the heart and lungs and carry out respiration. The ying-qi seeps out its fluids, pours them into the vessels, transforms them into blood, in order to nourish the four extremities, and internally pours into the five zang and six fu, in order to correspond to the counting of the [water-]clock markings.
